title: State Change After External Calls in claim()
description: The claim() function makes external calls to yield strategies before calculating/collecting payment. While ReentrancyGuard is active which blocks traditional reentrancy, the CEI (Checks-Effects-Interactions) violation may have edge cases where strategy callbacks cause inconsistent state.
impact: Potential inconsistent state if a strategy has non-reverting side effects that depend on or modify shared state. While direct reentrancy is blocked, cross-function reentrancy or read-only reentrancy patterns could still be exploitable.
attackPath: Deploy malicious yield strategy that performs callbacks
Strategy's claimYield() triggers external call to attacker contract
Attacker contract reads stale state or triggers other protocol functions
State becomes inconsistent due to ordering of operations
recommendation: Refactor claim() to follow CEI pattern: calculate all amounts and update state before making any external calls to yield strategies.
downgradeNote: Downgraded: CEI violation unexploitable due to EVM transaction atomicity and ReentrancyGuard

metadata.downgradeReason: PoC proved unexploitable due to EVM atomicity
